message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points (Texas) | |-------|--------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type:
 • Interstate/Freeway: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph in rural areas).
 • State highways: 55–70 mph.
 • Rural roads: 45–55 mph.
 • Urban streets: 25–35 mph.
• Speed limit signs are mandatory; failure to obey can result in fines and points. | | **Seat‑Belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and front‑seat passengers must wear seat belts.
• Rear‑seat occupants must use seat belts or approved child restraints.
• Failure to buckle up can lead to a $50 fine and 1 point on the driver’s record. | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) limit: 0.08 % for drivers ≥21 years old.
• Zero‑Tolerance for drivers <21 (any detectable BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, and possible jail time. | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Violations carry a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority.
• Stop signs require a full stop; failure to stop can result in a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children, regardless of direction.
• Failure to stop can lead to a $100 fine and 2 points. | | **Lane Discipline** | • “Lane discipline” law: Drivers must stay in their lane unless turning or passing.
• Improper lane changes can result in a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Parking & Loading Zones** | • Parking in loading zones, fire lanes, or handicap spaces without proper permits is illegal.
• Violations can incur fines ranging from $50–$200. | | **Points System** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 12 points within 3 years can lead to license suspension.
• Points are removed after 3 years of no violations. | | **Toll Roads** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., Sam Houston Tollway, Dallas North Tollway).
• Toll rates vary by vehicle type and time of day. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV).
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection (except in some counties). | --- ### Where to Find Official Information | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** | Official rules, licensing, registration, and penalties. | | **Texas Transportation Code** | Full legal text of all traffic laws. | | **Texas Highway Patrol** | Enforcement details, safety tips, and updates on new regulations. | | **Texas Transportation Commission** | Oversight of transportation policy and funding. | --- ### Quick Tips for Texas Drivers 1. **Always Check Speed Limit Signs** – Texas speed limits can change frequently, especially near construction zones. 2. **Use Hands‑Free Devices** – If you need to talk or use GPS, keep your hands on the wheel. 3. **Keep Your Vehicle Inspected** – Avoid costly fines by staying compliant with the annual inspection requirement. 4. **Know the Points System** – Even minor infractions can add up; consider a defensive‑driving course to reduce points. --- #### Need More Detail? If you’re looking for specific statutes, recent amendments, or want to know how a particular violation is penalized, let me know! I can pull up the exact section of the Texas Transportation Code or provide links to the TxDMV’s penalty tables.
